sources.title: Stabilize MacBookPro13,3 hardware support
sources.author: monomyth
sources.body:
## Summary

Add model-specific hardware support for the 2016 15-inch `MacBookPro13,3`. Wi-Fi and T1 have positive hardware results; the Radeon workaround has a subsequently reproduced failure and remains experimental:

- Install separately calibrated BCM43602 NVRAM so 5 GHz Wi-Fi is available.
- Install package-backed, freeze-safe T1 Touch Bar support.
- Add an experimental Radeon Pro 460 MCLK watchdog: keep VRAM at its highest DPM level while allowing core and PCIe scaling. This passed short tests but did not prevent a later unrecovered GPU hang; it is not a complete stability fix.
- Fix the existing MacBook NVMe suspend workaround so it follows the actual NVMe root device rather than hard-coding PCI `01:00.0`, which is the Radeon on this model.

## Dependencies

This is intentionally a stacked draft:

- Depends on #7671 for the shared atomic BCM43602 NVRAM installer. This branch adds the separate MacBookPro13,3 calibration; it does not widen attachment 290569's model gate.
- Depends on omacom/omarchy-pkgs#298 for `apple-ib-drv-dkms`.

Do not merge this draft until both dependencies land. After #7671 merges, the branch should be rebased onto current `quattro` so the shared dependency commits disappear from this PR.

## Validation correction — 2026-09-05

The short Radeon tests below are historical results, not evidence of sustained stability. On 2026-09-04, with the watchdog service active on `7.2.2-arch1-1-mbp133`, display power was enabled at approximately 17:49:02 PDT. At 17:49:09 the kernel identified OrbbecViewer in a graphics-ring timeout. Reset lost VRAM and failed during SMU firmware reload (`GPU Recovery Failed: -22`). Timeouts continued after the viewer stopped; the host remained SSH-accessible with mostly idle CPUs but blocked graphics work until reboot.

This disproves the earlier blanket claim that the watchdog prevents Radeon hard lockups. It does not isolate a cause among rendering, display-power transitions, watchdog timing, or other driver behavior. The later lid-close/open wake failure also remains unresolved. Keep this PR draft; dependency merges alone are not sufficient for readiness. The newer custom 7.2.3 installation has now been reconciled with the on-host task; its limited validation and separate local changes are described below.

## Additional validation on custom 7.2.3 — 2026-09-05

Live SSH confirms `7.2.3-arch1-2-mbp133`. The on-host audit verifies installed matching kernel/headers, matching loaded i915/AMDGPU/CS8409/iBridge/Touch Bar modules, and matching canonical/fallback UKIs. These are boot/load/integrity results, not a fresh functional test of every device.

- **Wi-Fi:** a live 5.6 GHz / 80 MHz connection with traffic and the same intended stable local MAC as the 7.2.2 test; reported link rates were 866.6 Mb/s RX and 702 Mb/s TX. This remains MacBookPro13,3-specific evidence.
- **Radeon:** at the September 5 test, the installed apply helper and monitor matched the then-current PR implementation; the subsequent recovery-loop correction is described below. With MCLK pinned at 1270 MHz and the unchanged watchdog active, official OrbbecViewer 2.9.3 used Radeon rendering for Color+Depth at 848x530 / 30 FPS for 60.27 seconds. CPU averaged 36.62% of one logical CPU, peak RSS was 493,522,944 bytes, and no matched GPU/USB/UAS/hung-task/panic/OOM event, coredump or watchdog restart was recorded. The viewer stopped its streams and exited cleanly.
- **Limits:** that one-minute pass does not erase the earlier failure, establish long-term stability, or attribute improvement to the kernel. The earlier software sample used four streams and a different measurement interval; this is not a controlled “8x speedup” result.
- **Intel:** a later Intel-rendered Color+Depth test failed with a blue display and required a power cycle. Retained logs did not establish the unique cause. Intel is disabled in the local Orbbec launcher; no repeat test is proposed.
- **Suspend:** the failed deep/s2idle platform-stage tests and the successful lock/blank/open/unlock containment cycle occurred on 7.2.2. On 7.2.3, only the installed safe-lid policy has been verified so far. This policy avoids kernel suspend and leaves the machine awake when closed, with power/thermal implications; it is not a suspend repair.
- **Separate local work:** the custom kernel forward-port, safe-lid policy, crash-collector repair and Orbbec renderer/scaling changes are not included in this PR. The scoped source comparison found no changes in the compared AMDGPU/i915/ACPI/power paths between the custom source trees; it does not prove all kernel behavior is identical.
- **Subsequent user confirmation:** the owner reported working T1, audio playback, and audio recording/video tested in Zoom on the 7.2.3 setup. This is user-reported functional evidence, not a claim that every individual key or audio mode was retested. Broader controlled Radeon validation is still outstanding. Do not routinely repeat the known-failing platform suspend or Intel camera tests.

### Additional installer issue found during follow-up

This defect was reproduced before the September 7 reconciliation: calling the old stable-MAC helper with an empty or nonexistent machine-id succeeded with the same `02:dd:27:89:9c:fa` result in both cases (isolated helper reproduction; no firmware writes). The old code hashed the salt even when identity was absent. The September 7 update below now rejects this input and adds regression coverage. This reproduction was evidence of a fallback collision, not a two-machine RF test.

## AMDGPU recovery-loop correction — 2026-09-06

OpenAI Codex identified and fixed a second failure mode in the watchdog from retained on-host journal and AMDGPU devcoredump evidence. During an Omarchy screensaver-to-lock transition, the Radeon gfx ring timed out in a Quickshell render thread. The kernel's PCI-config reset then stalled in ATOM BIOS execution and ended with `GPU Recovery Failed: -22`. Once the GPU controls returned `EBUSY`, the watchdog treated every unreadable state as a lost MCLK mask and reran the full apply helper every two seconds. That produced 300 additional gfx timeouts, 301 devcoredumps, and 322 failed MCLK retries before the host was power-cycled.

Commit `fc12fcad` contains the aftermath: DPM reads now distinguish a changed mask from an I/O failure, the apply helper is bounded to ten seconds, and any unreadable control or failed apply stops the watchdog cleanly until its next service start. The pre-display-manager MCLK pin and healthy reset-window monitoring remain unchanged. A focused regression test proves the monitor makes exactly one failed apply attempt and exits successfully instead of entering a retry storm; the complete shell suite reached all tests, with only the four companion-checkout coverage tests unavailable in this isolated worktree.

This contains the failure after it begins; it does not claim to fix the underlying Radeon/ATOM BIOS reset bug. The local safe-lid policy remains required because the same incident was compounded by a later lid-triggered s2idle attempt while Quickshell tasks were already blocked in the failed GPU reset.

## Reconciliation and validation — 2026-09-07

Commit `b58595f2` merges #7671 through `c0fea4e9` without rewriting the existing watchdog history. Both supported model families keep the required `macaddr=` key populated; neither persists the shared firmware placeholder when a unique fallback is needed. MacBookPro13,3 retains its established `mbp133-wifi` salt, while 14,2/14,3 use upstream's `bcm43602-wifi` salt. Existing installed calibration files remain untouched.

The helper now rejects missing, empty, malformed and all-zero machine IDs, propagates hash failures, and validates digest output. Tests cover exact historical addresses, deterministic reruns, distinct IDs, local/unicast bits, no-write failure, migration retry, a missing source MAC key, and rollback after a failed second rename. Cloned machine IDs still produce the same fallback by design; images must initialize distinct machine IDs. No claim of mathematically collision-free addressing is made.

Validation on an isolated Isengard checkout: `bash test/all` passed the CLI suite and **all 190 shell test files**, with the package and ISO companion checkouts. The focused T1 integration suite also passed with the updated #298 package. Tests used temporary firmware/sysfs/service fixtures; no installed Wi-Fi configuration was rewritten and no live radio reload occurred. The original `fc12fcad` watchdog implementation and its recovery-loop regression were preserved.

The on-host task has separately installed a health-gated s2idle policy and recorded a successful controlled cycle on September 6. This supersedes the earlier local no-suspend policy but is **not part of this PR**, not a claim that the underlying Radeon reset problem is fixed, and was not retested during this reconciliation. The custom kernel and other local suspend preparation remain separate work. This PR stays draft pending dependencies, maintainer review and broader stability validation.

## Hardware validation

Test machine:

- MacBookPro13,3, 2016 15-inch
- Intel HD 530 + Apple Radeon Pro 460/Baffin (`1002:67ef`, subsystem `106b:0160`)
- BCM43602 (`14e4:43ba`, subsystem `106b:015a`)
- Apple T1 iBridge (`05ac:8600`)
- Custom Arch `7.2.2-arch1-1-mbp133` kernel for the historical results below
- Omarchy Quattro
- Root filesystem on an external USB SSD; internal Apple NVMe is present but not the boot device

### BCM43602

MacBookPro13,3 uses kernel.org Bugzilla attachment 285753 rather than the 14,2/14,3 attachment in #7671. The installer supplies the host regulatory country and replaces Broadcom's placeholder MAC with a stable locally administered address.

Before: Band 1 only, connected at 2412 MHz.

After:

- Band 2 channels 36–165 available.
- Connected at 5600 MHz/channel 120.
- 866.6 Mbit/s RX and up to 866.6 Mbit/s TX.
- 20/20 gateway pings, zero loss; user speed test normal.

### T1 Touch Bar

- `apple-ib-drv-dkms 0.3.0-1` package-backed boot passed on the 7.2.2 custom kernel.
- `skip_acpi_power=1`; kernel confirms `ASOC.SOCW(1)` was not executed.
- Esc, volume, brightness, playback, and Fn/F1-F12 controls work.
- iBridge remains in USB configuration 1 with `power/control=on`.
- FaceTime HD camera captured 1280x720 MJPEG and worked in Zoom.
- Internal microphone captured stereo 48 kHz audio.
- DKMS also builds and installs for `6.18.49-1-lts`, but LTS was not boot-tested.

### Radeon

Unrestricted power-state transitions reproduced `VM_CONTEXT` faults and `sdma0`/`sdma1` ring timeouts followed by VRAM loss, SMU reload failure, and unrecoverable blue/black screens. `amdgpu.dpm=0` and `amdgpu.vm_update_mode=1` were not fixes.

Pinning only MCLK at 1270 MHz passed the trigger and repeated-video tests while SCLK returned to 214 MHz at idle. Hyprland resets the mask during session startup, so a fixed 45-second timer left a vulnerable window and reproduced the failure. The final watchdog:

- Applies synchronously before the display manager.
- Polls every 250 ms for the first 90 seconds, then every two seconds.
- Writes only after detecting that the driver reset the mask.
- Restored a simulated reset in 167 ms.
- Caught the real SDDM/session reset before Hyprland startup.
- Passed a 30-second trigger and 3.5-minute soak with zero GPU errors; idle returned to 59 C.

### NVMe targeting

The old service wrote `d3cold_allowed=0` to PCI `01:00.0`. On MacBookPro13,3 that is the Radeon; the internal NVMe is `02:00.0`. The replacement discovers controllers through `/sys/class/nvme` and applies only when the root disk is NVMe. External-USB roots disable and preserve the stale unit instead of touching either device.

## Tests

- `./test/cli` passes.
- All 190 `./test/shell` files pass with the required `omarchy-pkgs` and `omarchy-iso` companion checkouts present.
- New focused suites cover BCM43602 model/source selection, stable placeholder-MAC replacement, T1 production/recovery identities, package ownership, NVMe root-device discovery, exact Radeon board gating, and a simulated compositor MCLK reset.

## Custom 7.2.4 follow-up — 2026-09-15

Additional MacBookPro13,3 validation, with software versions kept separate:

- **Omarchy:** dev package `4.0.0.r2128.gb679363-1` (matching settings package).
- **Linux:** custom `7.2.4-arch1-2-mbp133`, with the existing gmux/VGA arbitration and CS8409 audio patches carried forward. This is not a stock-kernel result, and the custom kernel is not added to this PR.
- **Boot/install checks:** kernel and matching headers installed; canonical/direct UKIs matched, embedded kernel and encrypted external-USB-root command line verified, existing T1/panic add-ons retained, and a 7.2.3 recovery copy preserved. An attended reboot then confirmed the new running release and Hyprland.
- **T1:** unchanged `apple-ib-drv-dkms 0.3.0-4`, package integrity clean, DKMS rebuild/install successful, iBridge and Touch Bar loaded with matching vermagic and `skip_acpi_power=1`. The owner confirmed Esc/volume keys work.
- **Audio/camera:** patched CS8409 loaded; the owner confirmed audio playback, microphone and camera work after this reboot. This is functional confirmation, not a new resolution/sample-rate or every-mode test.
- **Wi-Fi:** existing 13,3 calibration files remain SHA-256 `a1a13fe89cf570ce94237cd27de36030584e8ec7084c3447c20c4fd668411dba`. Connected at 5600 MHz / 80 MHz; reported RX/TX link rates 866.6/585 Mbit/s, not throughput measurements.
- **Graphics:** watchdog active with zero restarts, manual mode and 1270 MHz MCLK. No matched GPU timeout/reset or storage I/O/Btrfs error in the immediate post-boot check; no failed system/user units.

**Limits:** suspend/resume was not tested on 7.2.4. The separately installed lid-wake DKMS module built for it, but that is not a suspend result. Long-term Radeon stability and controlled display-wake/graphics validation remain outstanding. The prior successful host-local s2idle evidence on 7.2.3 remains historical and outside this PR. Internal-NVMe-root operation was not tested; this host boots an external USB SSD. Keep this PR draft.

Also retaining the separate [13,3 Wi-Fi report from Johann-S](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/7671#issuecomment-5669775431): attachment 290569 with a per-machine MAC and the comment-97 `swctrlmap_2g` edit gave good 5 GHz results on their machine. They did not compare it against 285753 or test a 2.4 GHz join. We have not reproduced that alternative here, so it neither establishes a preferred 13,3 calibration nor validates widening #7671's 14,2/14,3 gate.

No PR code changed and no additional installer fixture tests were run for this update.

sources.title: Disable ghost internal display connectors
sources.author: piotrsynowiec
sources.body:
## Summary

- disable an empty duplicate internal `eDP-*` connector before modeless monitor recovery runs
- run that reconciliation on watcher startup, monitor hotplug/removal, and every Hyprland config reload
- retain the existing reload recovery for real modeless monitors, including external displays

## Problem

The modeless monitor recovery added in #6701 assumes that an enabled `0x0` output is a temporarily unavailable display whose modes may return after `hyprctl reload`.

On some dual-GPU laptops, the GPU that is not wired to the built-in panel exposes a second permanent eDP connector. Hyprland reports the real panel as a healthy `eDP-1`, while the unused connector can appear as an enabled `eDP-2` with:

- no description, make, or model
- no available modes
- a permanent `0x0` geometry

The generic monitor rule enables this output again after each configuration reload. Hyprland may then assign workspaces to the invisible output. The monitor watcher sees it as modeless and keeps reloading, but that connector can never acquire a mode. The result is an inaccessible workspace/window and an endless recovery cycle.

## Solution

Add a small hidden helper that disables an eDP connector only when all of these conditions hold:

1. another enabled `eDP-*` output has an identity, at least one mode, and non-zero geometry;
2. the candidate is enabled, has no identity, exposes no modes, and remains at `0x0`;
3. its connector name is safe to interpolate into Hyprland's Lua IPC expression.

The watcher invokes this helper synchronously before starting its existing modeless recovery loop. Once the permanent ghost is disabled, the modeless check no longer treats it as recoverable, so no reload loop starts. Running this after every config reload also makes the behavior survive package and system updates that reapply the generic monitor rule.

The conservative predicate intentionally does not disable:

- an external display that is temporarily modeless;
- the only internal connector;
- a deliberately disabled connector;
- an eDP connector with identity or advertised modes.

The logic does not depend on whether the real panel is numbered `eDP-1` or `eDP-2`.

## Verification

- `test/shell.d/monitor-modeless-test.sh` — passes, including new positive, negative, connector-numbering, Lua-safety, and watcher integration cases
- `bash -n` on both monitor helpers and the updated test — passes
- `git diff --check` — passes
- `./test/cli` — passes
- `./test/all` — the changed monitor tests pass; the local run ends with six unrelated environment-dependent failures (missing sibling `omarchy-pkgs` checkout, unavailable graphical runtime behavior, and sandboxed privilege/runtime paths). The two affected QR/disk-space tests pass when invoked directly with Bash.

`shellcheck` was not available on the test machine.

sources.title: Follow the T1 ambient light sensor for panel and keyboard backlight
sources.author: shawnyeager
sources.body:
## Why

macOS uses the T1 ambient light sensor for auto-brightness (Displays → Automatically adjust brightness, on by default). Once `apple_ib_als` is bound, Linux already exports IIO `in_illuminance_input` in lux. Omarchy only had keypress `brightnessctl`, so covering the camera cluster did nothing.

This is the userspace follow-on to the T1 driver work. It is not lid/DPMS persist, gmux persist, or the opt-in Studio Display stack.

## What

On MacBookPro13,2 / 13,3 / 14,2 / 14,3, a user unit follows illuminance while the lid is open and the internal panel is on:

- Panel via `omarchy-hw-display` (gmux on 15-inch, intel_backlight on 13-inch). Floor 8%.
- Keyboard backlight inverse of lux; off at 250 lux and above.
- Closed lid: skip, so lid-close overlays own the panel.
- Internal DPMS off: skip. The ALS sits in the camera cluster; a blanked panel drops lux, so following it while the display is off writes a dimmer target and that is what you see on wake.
- Toggle: `omarchy toggle als brightness` (also Trigger → Hardware → Auto Brightness). Flag `~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/auto-brightness-off` — presence means off, matching other Omarchy toggles. Default is on, like macOS.
- Non-T1 DMI or no IIO node: unit stays inert (`ExecCondition` + `ConditionPathExistsGlob`).

First-run and a DMI-gated migration enable the unit. 13,1 / 14,1 are not T1 and are not in the detector.

Without `apple_ib_als` the IIO node never appears, so this stays dark until that driver is loaded.

Companion package change: [omacom/omarchy-pkgs#315](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy-pkgs/pull/315).

## Test plan

- [x] `test/shell.d/t1-als-brightness-test.sh` (detector, hook, unit, migration, curve 170→42%/81, dark 8%/255, bright kbd 0, lid closed no-op, DPMS-off no-op, auto-brightness-off no-op, Hardware menu entry)
- [x] packaged unit path in `test/shell.d/config-test.sh`
- [x] MacBookPro14,3: live lux 170 → gmux 430/1023 (42%), kbd 81/255

## Related

Related: #7064
Related: #8025

#8025 is opt-in IIO auto-brightness aimed at Apple Studio Displays (USB ALS `05ac:1114`), panel only, with a Display-panel toggle. It does not default-on for T1, does not drive `spi::kbd_backlight`, and does not skip a closed lid or DPMS-off internal panel.

sources.title: Enable speakers on Late 2015 21.5-inch iMacs
sources.author: inspiretelapps
sources.body:
## Summary

Late 2015 21.5-inch iMacs (`iMac16,1` / `iMac16,2`) drive four digital CS4208 speaker channels. Analog Stereo is the headphone DAC and HDMI is the internal display, so both look like valid outputs while the speakers stay silent. Master hardware volume also does not change speaker loudness, so the Omarchy output slider moves with no audible change.

This installs a DMI-gated WirePlumber drop-in that:
- selects Analog Surround 4.0 on the CS4208 card
- uses software volume (`api.alsa.soft-mixer`)
- deprioritizes HDMI so it does not steal the default sink

Same shape as the ASUS ROG audio mixer quirk. Does not overlap with the CS8409 DKMS work for 2016–2019 Macs.

## Hardware

Verified on **iMac16,2** (Cirrus Logic CS4208, codec subsystem `0x106b8100`) on linux 7.1.9 / Omarchy 4.0.2: YouTube silent on Analog Stereo and HDMI, plays on Analog Surround 4.0; system volume slider works after software volume.

## Test plan

- `bash test/shell.d/imac-cs4208-speakers-test.sh`
- `./test/cli`
- On iMac16,1 or iMac16,2: install / migrate → `omarchy restart audio` → speakers play, output slider changes loudness
- Other hardware: hook and migration no-op

sources.title: Wake the panel when a laptop-only lid opens
sources.author: codemonkey76
sources.body:
Fixes the gap reported in #10170, whose analysis this follows.

The lid-open binding runs `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell`. That reconciler dispatches a DPMS enable only from `enable_internal()`, behind `if (( changed ))` — true only when a clamshell flag file was just removed. **The flag is never written when there is no external monitor**, so on a laptop-only machine the reconciler runs and dispatches nothing.

Meanwhile `lock/Service.qml`'s `idleBlankTimer` blanks the panel five seconds after a lid-close lock. So a laptop-only lid resume returns to a dark screen with no path back. Only `Keys.onPressed` on the lock screen's password field reaches `omarchy-system-wake`, and logind swallows the power button (`10-ignore-power-button.conf`) — so the machine looks hung to anyone who reaches for the power button rather than typing.

## The fix

Bind lid open to `omarchy-system-lid-open`, mirroring the existing `omarchy-system-lid-close`: reconcile first, exactly as before, then wake.

The wake had to stay a no-op when nothing is dark — `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal`'s `recover()` warns that an unconditional wake "undoes lock-screen blanking and races the resume modeset into a visible flash", and the clamshell watcher polls the reconciler every few seconds. Two things keep that true here: the wake sits on a lid-switch **event** rather than in the polled reconciler, and `omarchy-brightness-display on` already exits early while every enabled monitor reports `dpmsStatus` true.

## Test plan

- [x] New `test/shell.d/lid-open-test.sh` asserts the handler reconciles first, then wakes, and does nothing else. Verified non-vacuous — dropping the wake line fails it with "second call was none".
- [x] `test/shell.d/monitor-recovery-test.sh` updated for the new binding.
- [x] `./test/all` — the only failure is `bin-style-test.sh`, which fails identically on the base commit (raw `command -v` in the AI app removers, fixed separately in #10460).
- [x] Hardware A/B on a laptop-only machine (Intel CometLake-H + NVIDIA hybrid, `eDP-1` only, deep S3), blanking the panel exactly as the lock screen does:

```
blanked (as after lid-close lock): [{"name":"eDP-1","dpmsStatus":false}]
after omarchy-system-lid-open   : [{"name":"eDP-1","dpmsStatus":true}]

blanked again                   : [{"name":"eDP-1","dpmsStatus":false}]
after monitor-clamshell alone   : [{"name":"eDP-1","dpmsStatus":false}]   <- current binding
```

Scope note: this machine hit a dark panel on an 11-hour lid-closed resume (lid closed 19:07:14, opened 06:32:06, no external monitor), which is what led here. The structural gap above is confirmed and fixed. I can't prove it was the *only* cause of that particular incident — one observation from it recorded `dpmsStatus: 1` while the panel was dark, and I can't now reconstruct whether that reading was taken before or after a manual `dpms enable`. If a compositor-vs-hardware desync also exists on this hardware, it is a separate bug and this does not address it.

sources.title: Enable first-run user units one at a time
sources.author: fresh3nough
sources.body:
## Summary

Fixes #10484.

`install/user/first-run/enable-user-units.sh` ran a single multi-unit:

```bash
systemctl --user enable --now \
  bt-agent.service \
  ... \
  omarchy-crash-watch.service
```

under `set -euo pipefail`. `systemctl enable` validates the **entire** list before applying any unit. One missing unit (the reporter hit this with a package that never installed `omarchy-brightness-keyboard-auto.service` into `/usr/lib/systemd/user/`) fails the call, aborts the script, and leaves **every** later omarchy user unit disabled — bt-agent, sleep-lock, fcitx5, crash-watch, migrate-notify, recover-internal-monitor.

### Change

- Enable/start each shipped unit in a loop
- Warn on individual failure; continue
- Exit non-zero only if **none** of the units could be enabled

Note: this tree does not currently ship `omarchy-brightness-keyboard-auto.service` under `default/systemd/user/` (the reporter saw it only under `/usr/share/omarchy/...` on an older package build). The blast-radius fix is still required so any future missing unit cannot disable the rest.

## Evidence

### Bug reproduced (source + systemctl semantics)

```
# pre-fix script
set -euo pipefail
systemctl --user enable --now a.service missing.service
# → Failed to enable unit: Unit missing.service does not exist
# → under set -e, nothing after runs; a.service never enabled if it wasn't already
```

### Fix validated

```
bash test/shell.d/enable-user-units-test.sh
ok - enable-user-units enables units one at a time
ok - enable-user-units continues after a missing unit
ok - multi-arg enable fails the whole list when one unit is missing
ok - enable-user-units enables every shipped unit when all exist

bash test/shell.d/systemd-test.sh
# still green
```

## Test plan

- [x] Stub harness: missing mid-list unit still enables later units
- [x] Stub harness: all present → quiet success
- [x] Contrast: multi-arg enable fails whole list
- [x] `bash test/shell.d/systemd-test.sh`
- [ ] Manual first-run / re-run enable-user-units with a deliberately missing unit name

sources.title: Use active external displays for the lid-close lock decision
sources.author: yashranaway
sources.body:
## What changed

Use Hyprland's active external-monitor check when deciding whether a lid close should lock the session. Keep the physical connector detector unchanged for callers that need it.

On T2 Macs, tiny-dfr exposes a permanently connected Touch Bar DRM connector that Hyprland does not manage. The physical connector check treats it as an external monitor and skips the lock even when the laptop has no usable external display. This also makes the lock decision match the active-display check used by clamshell reconciliation.

Fixes #10618.

## Testing

- `bash test/shell.d/lid-close-test.sh`, including the real monitor-query helper with the reporter's internal-only monitor list and a positive physical connector check
- `bash -n bin/omarchy-system-lid-close`
- `git diff --check`

No T2 hardware or graphical session was available; physical lid-close verification is still needed.

sources.title: Avoid lspci in favor of sysfs
sources.author: neheb
sources.body:
## Summary

Replace every `lspci` call with reads from `/sys/bus/pci/devices` via a small shared helper (`install/helpers/pci-sysfs.sh`). `lspci` reads PCI config space, which forces the kernel to runtime-suspend a device that has entered D3cold — on hybrid laptops this means a bare `lspci` can take over a second waking the discrete GPU. The cached sysfs fields (`vendor`, `device`, `class`, and the `driver` symlink) never touch config space, so nothing wakes.

## Motivation

On hybrid laptops the discrete GPU idles in D3cold, and reading PCI config space forces a resume. This pays the wake penalty during config soaks and per-user setup, at the worst time in the boot/install flow. The vendor, device, class, and bound-driver information is already available from sysfs files the kernel caches — nothing there touches the device.

## What changed

**New shared helper** — `install/helpers/pci-sysfs.sh`:
- `omarchy-pci-id <vendor> [device ...]` — match by vendor + device ID
- `omarchy-pci-class-vendor <class> <vendor>` — match by class prefix + vendor
- `omarchy-pci-class-count <class>` — count devices with a given class prefix
- `omarchy-pci-driver <driver>` — match by bound driver symlink

All matchers walk `OMARCHY_PCI_DEVICES_PATH` (defaulting to `/sys/bus/pci/devices`); tests point it at a fixture tree.

**Hardware detectors migrated** (14 files):
- `bin/omarchy-hw-hybrid-gpu` — GPU count via `omarchy-pci-class-count 0x03`; also adds a `timeout` guard around `supergfxctl` so a wedged daemon no longer blocks the menu
- `bin/omarchy-hw-nvidia` (new) — NVIDIA GPU detection via `omarchy-pci-class-vendor 0x03 0x10de`
- `bin/omarchy-hw-intel-sof` (new) — Intel SOF audio DSP detection via `omarchy-pci-class-vendor 0x04 0x8086`
- `install/hardware/vulkan.sh`, `install/hardware/pacman.sh`, `install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh`, `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`, `install/hardware/fix-bcm43xx.sh`, `install/hardware/fix-yt6801-ethernet-adapter.sh`, `install/hardware/intel/fix-wifi7-eht.sh`, `bin/omarchy-install-gaming-gpu-lib32` — all migrated to sysfs matchers

**Nouveau cursor fix** — `install/user/hardware/fix-nouveau-cursor.sh` now uses `omarchy-pci-driver nouveau` instead of `lspci` output, and no longer needs a guard that checked whether `lspci` was available (sysfs is always there).

**Migrations** — `migrations/1784401744.sh`, `migrations/1785944594.sh`, `migrations/1786391100.sh` updated to use the sysfs helpers.

## Why lspci hurts on hybrid laptops

The kernel exposes PCI config space through `/sys/bus/pci/devices/<slot>/config`, and reading that file triggers a runtime resume if the device is suspended in D3cold. `lspci` reads config space for every PCI device it enumerates. On a hybrid laptop the discrete GPU typically sits in D3cold while the integrated GPU drives the display, so a single `lspci` call can force a >1 second wake — paid at the worst time: during config soaks and per-user setup. The `vendor`, `device`, `class`, and `driver` symlink in sysfs are cached by the kernel and served without waking the device.

## Files changed

| Area | Files | Net |
|------|-------|-----|
| New sysfs helper | `install/helpers/pci-sysfs.sh` | +69 |
| Hardware detectors | `bin/omarchy-hw-hybrid-gpu`, `bin/omarchy-hw-nvidia` (new), `bin/omarchy-hw-intel-sof` (new), `bin/omarchy-install-gaming-gpu-lib32` | +14 / -15 |
| Install scripts | `install/hardware/vulkan.sh`, `install/hardware/pacman.sh`, `install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh`, `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`, `install/hardware/fix-bcm43xx.sh`, `install/hardware/fix-yt6801-ethernet-adapter.sh`, `install/hardware/intel/fix-wifi7-eht.sh` | +81 / -23 |
| Nouveau fix | `install/user/hardware/fix-nouveau-cursor.sh` | +6 / -6 |
| Migrations | `migrations/1784401744.sh`, `migrations/1785944594.sh`, `migrations/1786391100.sh` | +16 / -8 |
| Tests | `test/shell.d/pci-sysfs-test.sh` (new), `test/shell.d/base-test.sh`, `test/shell.d/hw-hybrid-gpu-test.sh`, `test/shell.d/hw-nvidia-test.sh`, `test/shell.d/brcmfmac-supplicant-test.sh`, `test/shell.d/nouveau-cursor-test.sh`, `test/shell.d/t2-hardware-test.sh` | +137 / -46 |

**Total:** 24 files, +319 / -97

sources.title: Lock screen: keep fingerprint idle while the display is blanked
sources.author: niconistal
sources.body:
## Problem

- Once the lock screen blanks the display, the fingerprint PAM conversation stays armed and `fingerprintRetryTimer` re-arms it after every unsuccessful attempt, all night, even though nobody can touch the sensor with the panel dark.
- If the reader itself starts failing immediately, the retry interval is the failure interval: the lock screen opens a new `omarchy-lock-fingerprint` PAM session roughly every 300 ms.
- Both are pointless work against a device that cannot be reached, and a fingerprint backend left in that loop for hours can end up needing a power cycle before it verifies again.

## Change

- `runBlank()` suspends the fingerprint: it stops the retry timer and aborts the PAM conversation; `startFingerprint()` refuses to start while suspended.
- `runWake()` resumes it, so the prompt is armed again as soon as the display is up and the session is still locked with a fingerprint enrolled. A wake caused by the first keystroke of a password resumes the reader without touching the password in flight, and a panel coming back on its own (`onScreensChanged`) resumes it too.
- Unsuccessful conversations now reschedule through `scheduleFingerprintRetry()`. An attempt that ended sooner than a finger could have reached the reader compounds a failure streak and backs the next attempt off from 2 s to a 30 s cap; an attempt that lasted long enough to have been a real touch clears the streak and keeps the existing 250 ms retry. The display waking clears the streak as well.

## Behaviour

Before:

- Display blanked, still locked: a fingerprint attempt every retry interval until unlock.
- Reader failing instantly: a new PAM session about every 300 ms for as long as the lock is up.
- Waking the display changes nothing, because the reader was never stopped.

After:

- Display blanked, still locked: no fingerprint attempts at all.
- Reader failing instantly: attempts back off 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 16 s, then 30 s — about 1,400 attempts over 12 h instead of about 144,000.
- Waking the display re-arms the reader immediately and clears any backoff, so a recovered reader is live on the first touch.

## Motivation

On a MacBook Pro with Touch ID through the t1bridge fingerprint backend, after the laptop sat locked and blanked for hours, the backend was left in a bad state — its keybag relay service restarting continuously, "load biometric keybag failed" — until a power cycle. Password login was never affected. Separately, on 2026-09-10, once the backend started failing instantly ("Device reported an error during verify: fingerprint operation failed"), the journal shows about 180 fprintd verify errors per minute sustained for 12 hours, i.e. the lock screen opening a new PAM session roughly every 300 ms. Those are observations from one machine on one day.

The backend-side fault is being reported separately. This PR is only about the polling on Omarchy's side, which is worth avoiding on any fingerprint hardware.

## Testing

- `test/shell.d/lock-blank-fingerprint-test.sh` extended to cover the suspend/resume and the backoff; it fails on the unpatched `Service.qml`.
- `./test/shell` — 232 of 236 test files pass; the 4 failures (`config`, `locate`, `snapper`, `unowned-system-paths`) also fail on unmodified `origin/quattro` on this machine and are unrelated to the lock plugin.
- `qmllint shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml` — no new warnings against the pre-change baseline.
- No visual verification of this revision. An earlier revision of the blanked-display half was run on the owner's machine on 2026-09-07 and left locked overnight; this rebased revision, and the backoff, have only had the static checks above.

sources.title: apple: reload brcmfmac after resume, some Broadcom Wi-Fi parts don't survive S3
sources.author: TheoAndersen
sources.body:
Affects any Mac whose Wi-Fi brcmfmac drives over PCIe, but in practice mostly hits **older MacBook Pros**: BCM43602 (2015-2017 models) is the part most commonly affected. Reproduced on a **MacBookPro11,5 (15-inch MacBook Pro, Mid 2015, BCM43602)** simply by closing and reopening the lid, which is this machine's default S3 suspend/resume trigger.

The PCIe/msgbuf brcmfmac parts (BCM43602, BCM4350/4355/4364, BCM4377/4378/4387) can leave the firmware unresponsive after S3: every command times out (`brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd: Timeout on response for query command`) until the driver is unbound and rebound. Same signature and chipset family as Debian #849381, open since kernel 4.8, no real upstream fix.

Detection reuses the exact chip allowlist from `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh` (sourced from brcmfmac's own `brcm_hw_ids.h`), which deliberately excludes the BCM4360 in 2013-2015 Macs: it runs the out-of-tree `wl` driver instead of brcmfmac, so it never hits this bug. Scoping is three layers deep: the installer only runs on a T2 Mac or an Apple machine with one of these specific Broadcom IDs; the runtime helper re-scans for the same allowlist; and even then it only acts if the matched device is currently bound to `brcmfmac` — never touching anything else.

Unbind/bind is used rather than `modprobe -r`/`modprobe`: something (an open NetworkManager netdev, a cfg80211 wdev reference) reliably keeps the module in use across resume, so `modprobe -r` never actually removes it, and `modprobe` afterward is then a no-op that never re-probes a device manually detached via sysfs — confirmed on hardware, the device stayed unbound and Wi-Fi never came back.

A systemd unit runs the reload after every sleep target (suspend/hibernate/hybrid-sleep/suspend-then-hibernate), installed both on fresh setup and via a migration for existing installs. Covered by a shell test that simulates the sysfs unbind/bind cycle and exercises the T2/non-T2 detection matrix.

sources.title: Fix weak WiFi signal on BCM43602 (MacBook Pro 2015-2017)
sources.author: andyholst
sources.body:
## Problem

MacBook Pro 2015-2017 with BCM43602 (brcmfmac) gets **-90 dBm** signal — barely usable past 1 meter.

The root cause is the NVRAM config loaded by the brcmfmac driver is too generic. It lacks proper power amplifier settings and antenna gain parameters for the MacBook's hinge-antenna design.

## What Didn't Fix It

1. options brcmfmac feature_disable=0x82000 — fixes WPA handshake, NOT signal
2. options cfg80211 ieee80211_regdom=US — fixes regulatory domain, NOT signal
3. roamoff=1 — reduces scanning retries, NOT signal
4. NVRAM config from Andy Holst (Bugzilla #193121) — helps channels, NOT signal

All help with **connecting** but NOT **signal strength**.

## Fix

Install cristianmiranda's improved NVRAM config which has proper board flags, antenna gain, and power amplifier parameters specific to MacBookPro13,3:

- boardflags=0x02000001 — proper board configuration (BT coexistence, PALDO)
- boardflags2=0xC0000000 — LNA bypass for 2G/5G clip, spur WAR
- boardflags3=0x40000108 — RCAL WAR, FEM table from NVRAM
- pa2ga0, pa2ga1 — 2.4GHz power amplifier settings
- pa5ga0, pa5ga1 — 5GHz power amplifier settings (all chains)
- maxp2ga0=74 — max power limits
- agbg0=2, aga0=2 — antenna gain
- Correct MAC address substitution from the running interface

The NVRAM config file is bundled directly in the repo — no download needed at install time.

## Result

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Signal | -90 dBm | -58 dBm |
| 5GHz | Unusable | 360 MBit/s |

32 dBm improvement — 5GHz now works reliably at full speed.

## Changes

| install/hardware/apple/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt | The NVRAM config bundled in repo |
| install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-nvram.sh | Detects BCM43602, installs config, rebuilds initramfs |
| install/hardware/all.sh | Runs the new fix during hardware setup |
| migrations/1786391101.sh | Applies fix to existing Omarchy installs |
| test/shell.d/brcmfmac-nvram-test.sh | 18 tests, all passing |

sources.title: Scope the MacBook NVMe suspend fix to Apple's NVMe controller
sources.author: niconistal
sources.body:
`install/hardware/apple/fix-suspend-nvme.sh` disables D3cold on `0000:01:00.0` for every model in its regex, including the 15-inch MacBookPro13,3 and 14,3. On those two models `01:00.0` is the AMD GPU and the NVMe drive is at `02:00.0`. The file exists, so the check passes and the fix lands on the GPU. The drive is never touched.

From a MacBookPro14,3 on Omarchy 4.0.3:

```
01:00.0  [0300] AMD Radeon Pro 560 [1002:67ef]   d3cold_allowed = 0
02:00.0  [0108] Samsung SM961 NVMe [144d:a804]   d3cold_allowed = 1
```

The quirk comes from [Dunedan/mbp-2016-linux](https://github.com/Dunedan/mbp-2016-linux#suspend--hibernation), which scopes it to "models with Apple's NVMe controller (MacBookPro13,1, MacBookPro13,2, MacBookPro14,1 and MacBookPro14,2)". - **Leaf:** drop 13,3 and 14,3 from the model match. Apply the fix only when the device at `01:00.0` reports Apple's vendor ID `0x106b`, instead of just checking that a device exists there. The 12-inch MacBooks and 13-inch models keep the fix.
- **Unit:** the `ExecStart` path loses its `\:` escapes, which systemd logs as "Ignoring unknown escape sequences" on every boot. The written value is unchanged.
- **Migration:** existing installs where `01:00.0` is not Apple's controller have the service disabled and removed. The GPU goes back to its default at the next boot.
- **Test:** `test/shell.d/apple-suspend-nvme-test.sh` covers both the leaf and the migration, for every affected model and both 15-inch ones.

sources.title: Add omarchy-diagnose-suspend-wake
sources.author: ganjeez
sources.body:
## Summary
- Adds `bin/omarchy-diagnose-suspend-wake`, a CLI that finds which device is waking the machine early from suspend and offers a persistent fix.
- Relates to #1635: that thread has several people independently hand-diagnosing USB/Bluetooth devices that keep pulling their machine out of suspend (one report needed a second, different device disabled on top of the first fix). This automates the diagnostic process instead of trial-and-error guessing.

## How it works
- `status` — lists every device currently allowed to wake the machine (read-only, no root needed).
- `test [seconds]` — requests N seconds of real S3 suspend via the RTC alarm (`rtcwake -m mem -s N`) and reports whether it actually held that long. A device that wakes the machine early does so within seconds, well short of the requested duration.
- `diagnose [seconds]` — confirms the problem reproduces, disables every wake-enabled device as a control, confirms *that* holds sleep, then re-enables candidates one at a time until it's found every culprit (deliberately sequential rather than binary search — binary search only finds one culprit when there may be several, and a sequential pass costs about the same number of suspend cycles as a real candidate list has in practice). Offers to write a udev rule for whatever it finds.
- `restore` — undoes whatever a `diagnose` run left disabled, without touching anything that was off by firmware default to begin with (tracked via a state file, so it can't guess wrong).

## Testing
Built and validated this after using the same manual technique (`rtcwake` timing + sequential bisection over `/proc/acpi/wakeup` and per-USB-device `power/wakeup`) to actually find and fix a real instance of this bug — a MacBookPro11,4 whose internal Bluetooth controller was waking it from suspend all night, draining a full battery in 6-7 hours instead of holding sleep. Details and the confirmed device ID are in [my comment on #1635](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/1635#issuecomment-5674712503). Fixed with an overnight test after applying the equivalent of what `diagnose` now automates.

On top of that:
- `bash -n` clean, no syntax errors.
- `status` run against real hardware — correctly enumerates ACPI and USB wake-enabled candidates, correctly excludes a device already governed by an existing udev rule.
- The udev-rule-writing path verified via `udevadm test` in simulation mode against the real device — matches and writes the expected `power/wakeup: disabled`.
- `restore` and the interrupt trap verified not to touch devices that are disabled by firmware default (only ever act on the tool's own state-file-tracked set).

sources.title: Omit empty duplicate displays from the Display panel
sources.author: vincentritter
sources.body: The Display panel lists every connector Hyprland reports. On a dual-GPU laptop that includes outputs that cannot show a picture. The GPU that is not wired to the panel still exposes an eDP. Hyprland's catch-all `preferred` rule enables it at 0×0, with no EDID, no modes, and no make or model. The panel then draws a second row, checked as if it were a real screen. It is not the Touch Bar. Omarchy already treats an enabled 0×0 output as sick: `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-modeless` reloads until a mode appears. That recovery is for a monitor that powered on with a partial EDID. A permanent ghost never gets a mode, so reload cannot help, and the list stays wrong even after the connector is disabled by hand. #10198 disables those ghosts in Hyprland. This pull request filters the list. `omarchy-monitor-state` omits a connector that has no geometry, no modes, and no identity. A clamshelled laptop panel is also 0×0, but it still has EDID and modes, so it stays in the list and can be turned back on. A real HDMI you turned off is kept for the same reason. DRM names for these connectors swap across boots, so this does not key off `eDP-1` versus `eDP-2`. Hardcoding a port name would disable the laptop panel on the next numbering. `parseDisplays` also drops an enabled 0×0, so a live ghost cannot count as a second screen or let you disable the last real output. ### Before The stock Display panel on a T2 MacBook Pro (Intel + AMD). In this capture `eDP-2` is the laptop panel and `eDP-1` is the AMD eDP: connected, empty identity, no modes. ### After The same session, ghost still enabled in Hyprland. The panel no longer offers the empty connector, and the DISPLAYS section goes away because only one real screen remains. ### Tests `test/shell.d/monitor-state-test.sh` and `test/shell.d/monitor-test.sh` cover an enabled ghost, a disabled ghost, either eDP numbering, a clamshelled internal that must still list, and a user-disabled HDMI that must still list.

sources.title: Install stock kernel headers for broadcom-wl-dkms on upgraded Macs
sources.author: oliverox
sources.body:
Arch dropped the prebuilt `broadcom-wl` on 2026-09-02, and `broadcom-wl-dkms` carries `replaces=(broadcom-wl)`. On an upgrade, pacman swaps the package in and pulls `dkms`, but nothing pulls `linux-headers`, so the module never builds:

```
running '70-dkms-install.hook'...
==> ERROR: Missing 7.2.3-arch1-3 kernel headers for module broadcom-wl/6.30.223.271.
```

2012-2015 MacBooks with a BCM4360 or BCM4331 then come back from the Quattro upgrade with no driver bound and no Wi-Fi device at all. The installer's `fix-bcm43xx.sh` never runs on those machines, and `1789444024` only covers `linux-omarchy` and `linux-t2`.

`1789325478` will give `linux-omarchy` its headers, but it deliberately leaves the stock kernel installed as the boot fallback. On these Macs that fallback still has no Wi-Fi, which is usually the way back to a working system.

This migration installs headers for any installed Arch kernel (`linux`, `linux-lts`, `linux-zen`, `linux-hardened`) when `broadcom-wl-dkms` is present. The dkms pacman hook triggers on `usr/lib/modules/*/build/include/`, so installing the headers builds the module.

## Testing

- `test/shell.d/broadcom-wl-headers-migration-test.sh` covers the repair, idempotency, leaving `linux-omarchy` to its own migration, skipping machines without `broadcom-wl-dkms`, and propagating a failed install. It fails when the install line is removed.
- `test/shell.d/kernel-headers-migration-test.sh` and the other migration tests still pass.
- Verified on a MacBook (BCM4360, `14e4:43a0`) upgraded to 4.0.3 on stock `linux` 7.2.3. Installing `linux-headers` built `wl` through the hook, `modprobe wl` brought up `wlp3s0`, and NetworkManager connected.

sources.title: lock: re-arm fingerprint reader after a missed or errored scan
sources.author: slr01
sources.body:
# PR: Re-arm lock screen fingerprint reader after a missed/errored scan

File: `shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml` (lock plugin)

## What & why

One Quickshell `PamContext` is reused for the whole lock. After its first
session completes or errors, `fingerprintPam.active` never returns to false,
so `startFingerprint()` never starts another scan. Fingerprint unlock is at
most one attempt per lock — a single miss or driver error disables the reader
until you unlock with the password.

This change:

- Replaces the single `PamContext { id: fingerprintPam }` with a `Component`
  factory; each attempt creates a fresh instance (`fingerprintPamInstance`),
  so a miss/error no longer kills the reader for the lock.
- While the display is blanked (`runBlank`) it stops the retry timer and gates
  `startFingerprint()` on the existing `displaysBlank` state, so no new scan
  starts while blanked (without this some drivers, e.g. the Broadcom 58200
  TOD, scan continuously and hit a thermal self-disable). An in-flight scan is
  allowed to finish: aborting the pam session on blank severed a scan the
  reader was still servicing, and since the reader is not a compositor wake
  source that left it dead until password unlock.
- Re-arms on wake (`runWake`).
- Stops the fingerprint flow while a password prompt is in flight.

No new configuration is required. Behavior without a reader configured is
unchanged (`fingerprintConfigured` false → never started).

## How to apply

```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/quattro -b fix/lock-fingerprint-rearm
patch -p1 < lock-fingerprint-rearm.patch
git add shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml
git commit -m "lock: re-arm fingerprint reader after a missed or errored scan"
# push and open a PR against quattro
```

Validated on Omarchy 4.0.4 with a Broadcom ControlVault 3 reader
(`0a5c:5843`, fprintd 1.94.5): after a first-scan error, subsequent scans
succeed, including after a multi-minute locked+blanked period followed by wake.

## Suggested commit message

```
lock: re-arm fingerprint reader after a missed or errored scan

The lock screen reused one Quickshell PamContext for every fingerprint
attempt. Once its first session completed or errored, PamContext.active
stayed set, so startFingerprint() never started another scan: at most one
fingerprint attempt per lock, and a single miss disabled the reader until
password unlock.

Create a fresh PamContext per attempt via a Component factory, stop scanning
while the display is blanked (gating on the existing displaysBlank state) and
re-arm on wake, and suspend the fingerprint flow while a password prompt is
in flight.
```

sources.title: Debounce lid-close suspend so a quick reopen does not sleep in the dark
sources.author: ijt
sources.body:
Fixes https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/12193

## Why

logind's default `HandleLidSwitch=suspend` and Hyprland's lid bind both fire on the same close. A 2-second close/open then commits to S3 with the lid already open. `user.slice` is frozen, so Hyprland never sees `switch:off` and the panel stays at the lid-closed backlight. On this machine that looked like a hang and needed a power-button hold.

## What

- Packaged logind drop-in: `HandleLidSwitch=ignore` (and ExternalPower). Docked stays ignore.
- `omarchy-system-lid-close` still locks immediately, then starts `omarchy-system-lid-suspend`.
- That helper waits 3s (override `OMARCHY_LID_SUSPEND_DELAY`), then `systemctl suspend` only if the lid is still shut, there is no external monitor, and suspend is not toggled off.
- Lid open (`omarchy-system-lid-open`) cancels the pending job, runs `omarchy-system-wake`, and forces DPMS on. `omarchy-brightness-display on` can no-op when `dpmsStatus` is already true after S3 with backlight saved at 0.
- systemd-sleep `post` hook wakes the session 1s after thaw, because the compositor missed the lid event while frozen.
- Migration reloads logind once the drop-in is on disk.

## Not in this PR

The 20s delay used locally on a MacBookPro14,2. That number is because Alpine Ridge S3 resume is ~7s on that hardware (see the sibling Alpine Ridge PR). The portable debounce is 3s.

## Test plan

- Undocked: close lid 2s, open. Session locks, does not suspend, panel comes back.
- Undocked: close lid, leave closed. Suspends after ~3s.
- Docked: lid close stays awake on the external display.
- `omarchy toggle suspend` off: lid close locks, does not suspend.
- `./test/cli` and the lid-* / monitor-recovery shell tests.

Proven on Omarchy 4.0.2-1, MacBookPro14,2, kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2.

sources.title: Fix silent speakers on 12-inch MacBook (CS4208)
sources.author: teomurgi
sources.body:
## Problem

On the 12-inch MacBook (MacBook9,1 / MacBook10,1) the internal speakers are completely silent out of the box. Headphones work; every mixer looks fine; PipeWire shows an active sink — and nothing comes out. `manual/44-mac-support.md` currently lists "Sound is not functioning" as a known Mac limitation.

Additionally, once speakers do work, **audio dies after every suspend/resume** and only a reboot brings it back.

## Root cause

The Cirrus Logic CS4208 codec's speaker amplifier is never powered by the in-tree driver: the HDA controller reports a **generic PCI subsystem ID** (`8086:7270`), so `snd_hda_codec_cs420x` matches no Apple fixup and probes with `speaker_outs=0` (only the headphone jack `0x10` is wired through the analog DAC). Mainline has no working speaker config for this codec.

Four independent things are required for sound to actually come out — and stay out:

1. **The out-of-tree driver** — [leifliddy/macbook12-audio-driver](https://github.com/leifliddy/macbook12-audio-driver) replays the codec init (reverse-engineered from macOS) that powers the amp.
2. **The EFI startup chime un-muted** in NVRAM. The firmware only energises the class-D speaker amp when it plays the boot chime; if the chime is muted the amp is never powered and no software fix can work.
3. **Software volume** — the speaker path has no hardware amp volume (the codec's only analog amp is on the headphone path), so without a WirePlumber soft-mixer rule the volume slider does nothing.
4. **Suspend pinned to the freeze path** — s2idle kills the speaker amp (see "Suspend" below).

## Fix

Detect the two models and install all four pieces:

| File | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| `install/hardware/apple/fix-macbook12-audio.sh` | Gates on `MacBook9,1\|MacBook10,1`; clones + DKMS-builds the driver; installs the WirePlumber soft-mixer rule; clears the chime mute bit; installs a `sleep.conf.d` drop-in pinning suspend to freeze |
| `install/hardware/all.sh` | Runs the fix during hardware setup |
| `migrations/<ts>.sh` | Applies the same fix to existing installs (idempotent; removes the superseded d3cold service if present; sets `reboot-required`) |
| `test/shell.d/macbook12-audio-test.sh` | 14 tests, all passing |
| `manual/44-mac-support.md` | Documents the fix, the expected chime, and software volume |

## Suspend: what actually works (tested)

The obvious fix — pinning the codec out of D3cold, mirroring `fix-suspend-nvme.sh` — was implemented first and **disproven on real hardware**:

- With `d3cold_allowed=0` confirmed active at runtime, suspend/resume still killed the speakers. Post-resume codec state looked fully alive (stream attached, GPIO amp lines up, D0 power) yet no output.
- A codec reinit attempt (`echo 1 > /sys/class/sound/hwC0D0/reconfig`) was refused — PipeWire holds the device.

What works: writing `freeze` to `/sys/power/state` keeps the amp alive across suspend — audio verified working after resume. These machines have no S3 (the kernel rejects `freeze` for `/sys/power/mem_sleep`), so the drop-in sets:

```ini
[Sleep]
SuspendState=freeze
MemorySleepMode=
```

The empty `MemorySleepMode=` forces systemd (≥254) onto the plain-freeze path instead of probing `mem_sleep`. Verified end-to-end: `systemctl suspend` → wake → speakers work.

## Notes

- **The chime write** must be a single `write()` on an `O_WRONLY` fd — piping through `tee` fails with `Invalid argument` (`tee` uses `O_TRUNC` and the firmware attribute word is rejected). The migration and install script both use that form.
- **Packaging tradeoff:** the driver is installed by cloning and building against the running kernel (same template as PR #11620 for the CS8409). That runtime build downloads the matching kernel source tarball from kernel.org (~140 MB) at DKMS build time. If you'd rather host a `macbook12-audio-driver-dkms` package in the omarchy repo, the script collapses to a single `omarchy-pkg-add` — happy to switch.

## Tested

Verified end-to-end on a MacBook10,1 running Omarchy 4.0.4 / kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy: before the fix the sink ran at 91% with `speaker_outs=0` and silence; after it the DKMS `snd_hda_codec_cs420x` loads from `updates/dkms/`, the chime is audible at boot, the internal speakers produce sound with working software volume, and audio survives suspend with the freeze drop-in. `./test/shell` passes (6 unrelated pre-existing environment failures, unchanged with this commit stashed).

Refs #11619 (MacBook audio, CS8409) and #12217 (CS4208 woofers on MacBookPro12,1) — same class of model-gated hardware fix.

sources.title: apple: rebind brcmfmac across suspend
sources.author: teomurgi
sources.body:
## Problem

On Macs whose Wi-Fi is driven by `brcmfmac` (BCM4350 and relatives), a long suspend wedges the Broadcom firmware. After wake the kernel logs `brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd: Timeout on response for query command` for every request, NetworkManager sees `do-change-link: failure 5 (Input/output error)`, and the interface never recovers — only a reboot brings Wi-Fi back. Short suspends (seconds) resume fine; the failure shows up after hours asleep.

Observed on a MacBook10,1 (BCM4350, `14e4:43a3`): suspended 16:53, resumed 19:55, firmware dead from the first msgbuf command after wake.

## Fix

A `systemd/system-sleep` hook unbinds the Wi-Fi PCI device from `brcmfmac` before sleep and rebinds it after wake, forcing a clean firmware reload. NetworkManager then sees a fresh interface and reconnects on its own (~seconds after wake). Devices unbound at `pre` are recorded under `/run` and only those are rebound at `post`; a `post` with no matching `pre` is a no-op.

## Gating

Mirrors `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`: T2 Macs via the T2 PCI ID, older Macs via the `brcmfmac` PCI IDs from `brcm_hw_ids.h`. Hardware brcmfmac doesn't drive is left alone.

## Rollout

- New installs: `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-suspend.sh` runs from `install/hardware/all.sh`.
- Existing installs: migration installs the hook. No reboot needed — systemd-sleep runs every executable in `system-sleep` on the next suspend. Idempotent: an identical hook is left untouched, a locally modified one is refreshed.

## Tests

`test/shell.d/brcmfmac-suspend-test.sh` (13 assertions): hardware gating for the leaf and migration, idempotency, refresh of a modified hook, and the hook's own pre/post/no-op behavior against a stub sysfs. `brcmfmac-supplicant-test.sh` and `system-sleep-ownership-migration-test.sh` still pass.

sources.title: Ignore the Apple SMC power/lid device in the keyboard layout widget
sources.author: notabene00
sources.body:
On an Apple laptop Hyprland lists a third "keyboard" alongside the real one:

```
apple-spi-keyboard            layout: us,ru  active_layout_index: 1  (Russian)
apple-smc-power/lid-events    layout: us,ru  active_layout_index: 0  (English)
hl-virtual-keyboard-fcitx5    layout: us,ru  active_layout_index: 0
```

`apple-smc-power/lid-events` is the SMC power button / lid switch, the same kind of device `power-button` and `lid-switch` already are, but its name doesn't match `UNTYPED_KEYBOARDS`, so the widget counts it as a keyboard. It also announces `activelayout` *after* the real keyboard does:

```
activelayout>>apple-spi-keyboard,English (Macintosh, Russian-ISO)
activelayout>>apple-smc-power/lid-events,Russian      <- last, so typedKeyboardName lands here
activelayout>>hl-virtual-keyboard-fcitx5,Russian
```

so `selectKeyboard` pins the label to the lid switch, and a click on the widget switches the lid switch.

While every device sits on the same index that is invisible. It stops being invisible as soon as anything switches one device on its own — a layout-rewriting daemon, a per-device bind — because `switchxkblayout all next` then keeps the seat permanently one step out of phase. On my machine the bar showed exactly the opposite layout of the one I was typing in, and clicking it flipped the label without changing the keyboard.

Fix: list the SMC device with the ACPI buttons, and let `eventKeyboardName` reuse `isTypedKeyboard` instead of only skipping `hl-virtual-keyboard`, so a device nobody types on cannot become the one the widget follows.

Tested with `test/shell.d/keyboard-layout-test.sh` (two cases added) and on a MacBook Pro M1 running Hyprland.

sources.title: lock: stop fingerprint scans while the display is blanked
sources.author: slr01
sources.body:
## What and why

While a display is blanked, the lock screen keeps the fingerprint reader running scan cycles against an empty pad. On fingerprint readers that thermally self-disable (Broadcom CV3 / `0a5c:5843`, Goodix `27c6:533c`, Elan `04f3:0c4b`, all `libfprint-tod`), that cycles the driver into `Device disabled to prevent overheating` refusals: 31,534 `PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL` / code 9 returns in under four hours on a CV3, in a 205 s-refusing / 122 s-available cycle. Each refusal re-arms the 250 ms retry timer, so the reader stays in the storm.

This PR stops new scans while the display is blanked and re-arms on wake. With it, a CV3 logged **0 refusals across a 15-minute lock** and read on the first touch after wake ([measurement thread](/omacom/omarchy/pull/12201#issuecomment-5721534266)).

## Changes (3 lines-worth of gating, purely additive vs stock)

- `runBlank()`: stop `fingerprintRetryTimer` so a blanked display is not re-arming scan cycles
- `startFingerprint()`: return early while `displaysBlank`
- `runWake()`: re-arm a scan if a lock is active

No `abort()`: an in-flight scan is allowed to finish; on readers where `power/wakeup` is disabled, the reader cannot wake the compositor, so aborting on blank can strand it with nothing to re-arm it.

## Notes

- Composes with the libfprint temperature/backoff model in libfprint#7179 rather than colliding with it.
- Purely additive against `quattro`; no behavior change while the display is awake.

sources.title: lock: re-arm fingerprint reader with a fresh PAM context per attempt
sources.author: slr01
sources.body:
## Prerequisite

Depends on #12420 (lock/fingerprint-gating). This branch is stacked on that PR's branch, so this PR currently shows both commits; once #12420 merges into `quattro`, this PR automatically reduces to the factory change alone. Reviews of just the factory change are in the second commit (`c4291018`, `lock: re-arm fingerprint reader with a fresh PAM context per attempt`). The gating half is the load-bearing fix for thermally-self-disabling readers; this PR addresses a second, distinct failure mode.

## The failure mode

The lock screen reused one `PamContext` for every fingerprint attempt. When a session **started** (list query succeeded, "Place your finger…" relayed) but then errored mid-identification, `PamContext.active` stayed set and `startFingerprint()` bailed forever — the reader is dead until password unlock. This is separate from the fast `PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL`/code 9 path, where `start()` fails synchronously, `active` drops immediately, and stock re-arms on its own.

Repro capture (lock screen, packaged 4.0.4, Broadcom CV3):

```
15:01:45  identify()                              <- first (and only) session
15:01:55  Identification failed due to unforeseen error!
          (finger held for the next 60s: nothing, reader never re-armed)
```

## Changes

- `PamContext` becomes a `Component` factory; each attempt creates a fresh instance.
- `handleFingerprintFinished()` and `handleFingerprintError()` clear the instance reference and destroy it (`handleFingerprintError` via `Qt.callLater` — a synchronous destroy inside the error callback would happen inside the context's own lifetime).
- Lifecycle calls (`resetAuthenticationState`, password prompt in flight, fingerprint recheck after setup) route through `stopFingerprintPam()`.
- Includes the leak fix noted on the original thread: `createObject(root)` parents instances to `root`, and the old `handleFingerprintError()` dropped the reference without destroying, leaking a `PamContext` per errored attempt for the rest of the lock.

## Testing

Happy to test on CV3 once the split is in. The 15:01:45/15:01:55 capture is the standalone repro for this PR.

sources.title: Reclaim lock screen keyboard focus after resume from suspend
sources.author: jonathan-downs
sources.body:
## Summary

- The lock screen's password field only regrabs keyboard focus when `inputEnabled` toggles or when the user clicks/moves the pointer on the lock surface (`LockView`'s `wakeRequested`). A real suspend/resume does neither: the lock was already active before the machine slept, so `inputEnabled` never changes, and there's no pointer activity on resume. The surface comes back with no focused input, so nothing you type registers until you click the screen.
- Adds `omarchy-resume-focus-monitor.service`, a systemd user service mirroring the existing `omarchy-sleep-lock.service`, running `bin/omarchy-system-resume-monitor`. It watches logind's `PrepareForSleep` signal for the resume case (`boolean false`) and calls a new `lock` IPC verb, `resume()`, on each occurrence.
- `lock/Service.qml`'s `resume()` IPC handler calls a new `handleSystemResume()` that reuses `runWake()` and bumps a new `resumeSignal` property, wired into `LockView` so it reclaims focus the same way the click handler already does.

**Note on design:** my first pass ran the monitor as a plain QML `Process` owned by `Service.qml` instead of a systemd service. Testing on real hardware caught a real leak in that approach: when Quickshell itself is torn down (a shell restart, a crash-and-relaunch), the `Process`'s own child can be killed abruptly enough that its coproc'd `dbus-monitor` grandchild is orphaned rather than reaped, reparenting to the user's systemd instance and leaking a live system-bus connection indefinitely. Reproduced across multiple shell restarts before fixing it. The systemd-service approach here avoids that entirely: the whole unit's cgroup (dbus-monitor included) is torn down together regardless of how the service itself exits, matching the existing pre-sleep monitor's own approach for the same reason.

## Related

Encountered while investigating a report involving a suspend/resume-specific numpad quirk on the lock screen (separate root cause, not addressed here). This PR only covers the confirmed, reproducible focus issue. It touches the same file as a few other open suspend/resume + lock-screen issues, so linking for context in case of overlapping work:

- #11820
- #12140
- #11744

## Test plan

- [x] `./test/cli` - all passing
- [x] `./test/shell` - all passing except 5 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change and reproducible on a clean checkout (`config-test.sh`, `locate-test.sh`, `omarchy-kernel-migration-test.sh`, `snapper-test.sh`, `unowned-system-paths-test.sh`)
- [x] New `test/shell.d/resume-monitor-test.sh`: verifies the monitor calls `omarchy-shell lock resume` once per resume event while ignoring sleep events, cleans up its `dbus-monitor` producer when the pipeline itself is killed directly (bypassing systemd, to prove the script doesn't rely on systemd alone), and that `--consume` parses events correctly from stdin. Ran 5x in a loop with no leaked processes.
- [x] New assertions in `test/shell.d/systemd-test.sh` for the service file's `ExecStart` path, environment/ordering conditions, `Restart=always`, and that first-run enables it
- [x] Verified locally on real hardware via a plugin clone of `lock` plus the real systemd service: lid-close suspend/resume no longer requires a click before the password field accepts input, and confirmed zero leaked `dbus-monitor` processes across multiple shell restarts and service (re)starts

sources.title: Keep the keyboard backlight level across lock and suspend
sources.author: mohan314e
sources.body:
## What's wrong

The keyboard backlight goes off and never comes back. Turning it on by hand doesn't help — the next wake turns it off again.

## How it's meant to work

Locking blanks the backlight:

1. Remember the current level (`brightnessctl -s`)
2. Set it to 0

Waking puts it back:

3. Restore the remembered level (`brightnessctl -r`)

That is correct, as long as step 1 only ever runs while the light is actually on.

## Why it breaks

Step 1 remembers **whatever it finds** — including 0. So a blank that runs while the light is already off remembers 0.

After that, "restore the remembered level" means "set it to 0". Every time. Nothing ever writes a good value back, so it never heals on its own.

So the whole bug reduces to one question: **can a blank ever run while the light is already off?**

## Yes — and only one path does it

A blank is normally preceded by a wake, and a wake restores the light. So the light is on when the blank runs. Fine.

Four places schedule a blank:

| | what it is | wake before it? |
|---|---|---|
| `:146` | you lock the screen | yes — you were just using the laptop |
| `:181` | you touch the lock screen | yes — `runWake()` ran first |
| `:551` | a password attempt ends | yes — submitting called `runWake()` |
| `:490` | **resume from suspend** | **no** |

`:490` is the suspend gap. The blank countdown freezes during suspend. On resume it fires late, notices the gap, and re-arms — but it never wakes anything:

1. Before suspend: blank runs. Remembers 40, sets 0.
2. Suspend, then resume. The light is still 0.
3. `:490` fires and re-arms. No wake, so nothing restores the light.
4. Five seconds later the blank runs again. It finds 0. **It remembers 0.**

Poisoned, permanently.

Resume can't be rescued anywhere else either. `runWake()`'s callers are `:169`, `:218`, `:244`, `:298` and `:323`, and the last needs real typing or mouse movement on the lock screen. Opening a lid is neither.

**Fix 1 — `Service.qml:490`: wake, don't just re-arm.** `runWake()` arms the timer itself while locked, so the five-second run-up before blanking still happens. The light is simply real again before the next blank records it.

## A second, separate problem

Restore writes the remembered level no matter what. But the backlight hotkeys still work while locked. So if you set the level yourself on the lock screen, the next wake throws your choice away (#10767).

The level at restore time tells you which happened:

| level when restore runs | what it means | what to do |
|---|---|---|
| still 0 | nothing has touched it since the blank | the remembered level is still yours — apply it |
| anything else | it was set *after* the blank | that is newer than what we remembered — leave it alone |

The same rule also covers locking while the light was already off: remembers 0, sees 0, applies 0 — no change, no special case needed.

**Fix 2 — `restore` only writes while the level is still 0.**

This is also why `off` is left as-is. Guarding `off` against saving 0 would mean a backlight you deliberately turned off is never remembered, and the next wake would switch it back on.

**Fix 3 — `omarchy-system-wake` restores the keyboard before the display.** The display call goes through Hyprland IPC, which lid transitions can stall; the keyboard write goes straight to sysfs and is instant. Doing it first means it is already done if the display call hangs — and `runWake()` drops a new wake request while the previous one is still running.

`OMARCHY_LEDS_PATH` follows the existing `OMARCHY_BACKLIGHT_PATH` and `OMARCHY_DRM_PATH` seams, so the new test can run on hardware with no keyboard backlight.

Reported in #9339, #10105 and #7650.

**Validation:** the new `test/shell.d/brightness-keyboard-test.sh` covers blank/restore, a level changed while blanked, and a deliberate zero. It fails against the unpatched script and passes on this branch. `qmllint` reports no new warnings on `Service.qml`. `./test/all` passes apart from ten files that fail identically on a clean checkout in this environment for unrelated reasons. The three changes were also applied to a running 4.0.4-1 system and exercised through real blank and restore cycles; a full suspend and resume cycle was not manually tested.

sources.title: Stop counting Hyprland virtual outputs as external monitors
sources.author: HritwikSinghal
sources.body:
Fixes #8027.

## What goes wrong

Dock the laptop, turn the laptop screen off (SUPER + CTRL + Delete, or Hardware -> Laptop Display), then unplug the external monitor. The laptop is left with no screen at all until the next login.

## Why

When the last enabled monitor goes away, Hyprland creates a placeholder output named FALLBACK (FallbackStateKeeper, src/state/FallbackState.cpp, since 0.56.0). Nothing is behind it, but it reports `disabled: false` and its name is not eDP/LVDS/DSI, so `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active` answered "an external monitor is active".

Six callers use that answer to decide whether turning the laptop screen back on is safe, and all six back off: `off()` and `recover()` in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal`, `recover()` in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal-mirror`, `enable_internal()` and the dock check in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell`, and the poll in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-watch`. Only the next login recovers it, because `omarchy-recover-internal-monitor.service` asks `omarchy-hw-external-monitors` instead, which reads the kernel.

## The fix

Ask the kernel too: a real display has a DRM connector, a placeholder has none. Fixing the helper fixes all six callers at once.

Excluding the names FALLBACK and HEADLESS-* would also work today, but 0.55 called this same output HEADLESS-n and 0.56 renamed it, so the next rename would bring the bug back with nothing to notice it.

`monitors all` stays, so a mirrored external keeps counting. Any connector status except `disconnected` counts, because a connector with no working detect (VGA, DVI-I) reports `unknown` for a display that is genuinely attached.

## Measured on hardware

Dell XPS, Intel Panther Lake, eDP-1 plus a Dell AW3225QF on DP-1. Omarchy 4.0.0, Hyprland 0.56.2. Sampled 5 times a second across a real unplug:

| | placeholder visible | toggle flag | laptop screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1.75s | stayed set | never came back on its own |
| after | under 0.5s | cleared by the next sample | back immediately |

## Tests

New `test/shell.d/monitor-external-active-test.sh`, 11 checks. Against the current helper it fails at the first one:

    not ok - the FALLBACK output is not counted as an external monitor

Full suite: 7 of 246 files fail, the same 7 that fail on a clean quattro checkout (see #7125).

sources.title: Wake displays before restoring keyboard and clamshell state
sources.author: RenanBezerraGuima
sources.body:
## What

`omarchy-system-wake` ran three steps sequentially on every wake (idle activity and post-unlock):

1. `omarchy-brightness-display on` — lights the panels (user-visible)
2. `omarchy-brightness-keyboard restore`
3. `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell` — can take seconds on docked setups when it triggers `hyprctl reload`

Only step 1 is on the critical path. Steps 2 and 3 now run in the background, so the session is responsive as soon as the displays are lit. Ordering is preserved: DPMS enable still runs first.

## Side-effect fix

Both QML callers (`idle/Service.qml` `cancelIdleCycle`, `lock/Service.qml` `runWake`) skip a wake while a previous one is still `running`. A slow clamshell (with reload) used to hold the process open, so a second wake event during that window was dropped entirely — including its DPMS enable. With the script returning fast, every wake lights the display.

## Numbers (this machine: single eDP-1, no kbd backlight)

5 runs each, `omarchy-system-wake` wall time:

| | run1 | run2 | run3 | run4 | run5 | median |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (sequential) | 171ms | 153ms | 151ms | 151ms | 151ms | ~151ms |
| After (display foreground, rest background) | 38ms | 30ms | 33ms | 31ms | 31ms | ~31ms |

~5x faster here; on docked multi-monitor setups where clamshell reloads Hyprland config, the win is seconds, not milliseconds.

## Testing

- `bash -n bin/omarchy-system-wake` — clean
- `test/shell.d/monitor-recovery-test.sh` — all 18 checks pass (before and after), including "system wake resyncs clamshell display state"
- `test/cli` — passes (command metadata untouched)
- Manual: `omarchy system lock` → unlock lights the panel immediately; background jobs finish cleanly (`pgrep` shows nothing left behind); `hyprctl monitors -j` reports `dpmsStatus: true`; clamshell toggle state unchanged

## Out of scope (possible follow-up)

The synchronous `sleep 4` + `supergfxctl` transitions in the `force-igpu` system-sleep `post` hook also stall resume for Integrated-mode users, but changing it would break the synchronous expectations in `system-sleep-ownership-migration-test.sh`. Left for a separate PR.

## Problem

Typing a digit on the numeric keypad does nothing in the lock screen's password field. The same digit on the number row types fine. Anyone whose password has digits typed on the keypad has to toggle NumLock off and on at every lock (#8552).

## Cause

Qt never reads the compositor's NumLock state at startup (QTBUG-32687). Even with NumLock on, the keypad reaches the field as Home, Up, PageUp and the rest with `Qt.KeypadModifier` set and no text, and `TextInput` treats them as cursor movement.

Map those keys back to their digits in the field's key handler when `KeypadModifier` is set. Digits that already carry text, the top row and plain cursor keys are untouched, and nothing is inserted while the field is read-only during authentication.

Same approach as #10530 takes for the polkit dialog. The lock keeps its own model so the two can land independently; if both land, the two helpers can fold into one.
